"Maybe, maybe not. Yeh come with me, though, I’ll make things right for yeh." Caine leaned in close, his face twisting to an ugly snarl. "I’ll take care of that captain for your mum. Make it look like an accident and yeh get to keep yer promise. How’s that sound?"
Kell cocked his head. "You’d do that?"
"I’ve done worse."
"Yeah. I reckon you have." Kell nodded. "I’ll get my hat."

name: Name
body:
"No!" Cynthia screamed in pain. Lacerated over and again by black tendrils of withering darkness that Deneghra summoned to inflict excruciating agony through her body, she struggled against bonds that would not give an inch. The witch sisters watched on, admiring their master’s work with cruel delight.
In plain sight now, Cynthia could see the sisters against the backdrop of their workshop of horror: a mirrored patchwork of each other with only vaguely humanoid forms. Their faces were cowled, little more than glowing coals under bulbous hoods.
Their bodies appeared more machine than flesh, each with a single human leg surrounded by a cluster of spidery, mechanikal limbs, each ending in a cruel talon that scratched the stone floor when they skittered about. Each of them was covered in a hodgepodge of rags and a grotesque mechanikal augmentation that appeared to run uniformly down half their bodies in an arrangement that defied comprehension as to its purpose.
In places, mechanika apparatuses jutted from them like metal spines; in other places, clusters of catheter hoses trickled a revolting green sludge. They were hunchbacked with arcane turbines that glowed green with necrotite, and each had a collection of arms in addition to a single limp human limb. These additional spindly appendages were arrayed like the spines of an umbrella, ending in an assortment of tools and jagged blades.

name: Name
body:
Together and in clear view, the pattern suggested each sister was indeed a half of the other, their missing halves simply filled in with mechanika. That they might once have been human was irrelevant; they were now each something more and also something much less.
Deneghra paused her torment, watching Cynthia’s ragged breathing with cool calculation. Cynthia felt her mind probing too, felt the warwitch’s malignant magic drilling into her thoughts.
What the trio wanted from Cynthia during each of these ordeals was becoming clearer by intuition if not by explanation. As her physical reserves flagged against pain, against hunger, and against fear, she felt her Gift of magic flaring up. Indeed, at every touch of Deneghra’s burning tendrils, she felt power rising in her chest, nourishing her, ready even to give her the strength to retaliate. Yet she fought it back. It’s what they wanted; she knew it in her heart. If they wanted it, she would not give it to them.
Not yet at least.
Cynthia gasped during the momentary respite, her chin dropping to her chest as she hung limply on the torture rack she had been fixed to, hands and feet bound at opposite corners. Deneghra smiled and lifted Cynthia’s chin with a black-taloned finger, staring into Cynthia’s eyes in a manner most unkind as she leaned ever closer for inspection. Cynthia took the opening to spit in her eye.

name: Name
body: "You desire more?" Deneghra wiped the spittle with a smile, showing it to her. "That’s what you’re telling me?" "Do what…do…what…" As Cynthia’s strength faded, she began to sob softly. "Yes, that’s it." Deneghra turned to her retinue with a cruel smile. "Put another one in the box, ladies. She’s ready." *** From his cliffside perspective, Caine regarded the signalman at work on the docks below like an ant waving a torch in the dark. He then glanced up to the crenellated ramparts of the Sentinel Point Naval Fortress, which loomed over him like a row of teeth atop the sheer cliff. The ramparts were interrupted at fifty-yard intervals by jutting casemates served by heavy cannons, all trained on the new arrivals coming in. Between a rock and a hard place. Caine shook his head and climbed. Inside wouldn’t be much better. Thanks to Ace’s breakout in Caspia three days ago, what was already the most secure fortification in all Cygnar had now doubled its garrison at Rebald’s bidding. The reason was simple: Sentinel Point kept Hadley Gaynor’s prototype skyship the Wind Sabre under lock and key. Thanks to Caine’s plan that he’d shared with the war council, Rebald knew he needed it.

name: Name
body: "Impregnable" was the word Caine had used to describe Sentinel Point to Anastasia. At the time, she just smiled and drew him a map. Now here they were, scaling Sentinel’s south wall and very nearly inside. To be fair, Caine’s own Gift had allowed him to make his way into some very tight spaces in the past, but as the high winds buffeted him once more, he had to admit this particular infiltration was on a level he had not experienced. This was the talent that Rebald’s black book could buy, and it was a good test for what was to come in Skell. And with Bastian Falk still working from the inside, they might pull this off. Caine scanned the cliffs of the seawall, spying a Cygnaran battlegroup on approach to the heavily fortified south dock where the signalman stood. Out over the dark waters, he could see a bulky cruiser with a pair of lean frigates in escort. Though he could not read their names in the darkness, he already knew them as the Successor, Victorious, and Preeminence, all departed from the port of Caspia only a day ago.

name: Name
body: Aboard the cruiser Successor was a prized human cargo now under the careful watch of his man Falk. The stowaway gun mage had tracked down three engineers in service with a rare pedigree: certified air crew. There would be no flying the skyship without them, and of course, just as there would be no skyship without Anastasia. As Caine focused on the sea vessels, he missed his footing and slipped. For his mistake, a handful of pebbles tumbled into the gulf of Cygnar. "Watch it," Watts grumbled beneath him, his tricorn catching some of Caine’s pebbles. "Sorry, chum." Caine steadied himself with a wider stance, secured his grip before resuming climbing. The howl of wind filled his ears as he followed Anastasia upwards toward the entry point. On her map, she had drawn an iron exhaust grate hewn from the rock, two yards across. Now, here it was as promised, only another thirty yards climb to go. "Are we there yet?" Ryan scrambled up after Caine, the gleam of her alchemical goggles like a predator’s eyes in the night.

name: Name
body:
"Do they ever stop?" Anastasia peered past Caine while scaling the cliff as easily as walking. Her expression was one of cool curiosity.
"On occasion." Caine pulled himself up another few feet while trying not to look down. "Luckily, they shoot straight."
"I can bend a shot pretty good too, lady," Ryan suggested. "Whatever it takes to get the job done."
"Easy." Caine glanced down. "Anastasia here is taking time out of her busy schedule to help us."
"Yeah, a real kindness that," Watts chuckled.
Anastasia was already at the grate.
"Worth every penny." Caine joined her with a final push. "Been a while since I done anything like that."
As Watts and Ryan joined them on the perch of the grate’s lip, Anastasia put a hand out for Watts—or, more specifically, the sling pouch of tools he carried. "Cutters, please."
Watts took a deep breath and a wide look before producing the tool. "Hell of a view, eh?"
Ryan nodded, swinging her legs over the side to sit at the lip, peering all the way down to the crashing waves at the base of the cliff.

name: Name
body:
Behind them both, with two precise clips, Anastasia cut the padlock that secured the grate.
"Let’s go," she said in Llaelese, then she was inside and lost to shadow.
As the trio followed her into the ventilation shaft, they were forced to crouch beneath clusters of narrow pipes the length of the narrowing passage. As they went deeper, a faint glow and muffled sounds grew more distinct with each step. Ahead, the bottom of the shaft gave way to a steel grating that allowed a look down. This gave them a full view of a great hangar carved into the cliff’s natural caves.
The cavernous hangar was dimly lit with only a few overhead lights in operation. In the center of the hangar sat a large object covered in a burlap tarp with stencil markings. To Caine, it appeared the object was about fifteen yards long and half that wide.
"Is that it?" Ryan hissed.
"Or I’m a gobber’s uncle." Watts pointed. "Look at the shape of the stern. Does that look like Gaynor’s plans?"
"I reckon it could be," Ryan said.
Once again, Anastasia spoke in Llaelese. "Let’s get to it then."

name: Name
body: Her route had circumnavigated most of the active watch in the fortress above but certainly not all of it. Despite the hangar being in the very bowels of the coastal fortress, Caine spotted a squad of Cygnaran marines roaming the vast floor space, five in total, sometimes passing out of sight behind stacked crates, at other times talking casually amongst themselves. "Courtesy of Rebald," Caine said. "He never learns." "Remind me to thank him next time we meet," Watts said. "There’s an opening." Anastasia pointed ahead as the patrol below them moved out of sight. "Let’s go." Caine followed as Anastasia lowered a rope to the top of a stack of crates about fifteen feet below them. It chafed him not to invoke his magic, but it wasn’t worth the risk here, for the same reason he’d avoided it with Ace. One by one, they shimmied down the rope onto the crates then quickly dropped to floor level, where they converged in the shadows for a final huddle. "Make sure the mooring lines are untethered." Caine looked to a yard arm crane in the center of the chamber and next to the hangar doors exiting to the south dock. "Anastasia and I will clear a path to Falk and help him escort our aircrew back here."

name: Name
body:
"He’s sure about these guys?" Ryan asked.
"He’s sure they can pilot the thing." Caine scratched his chin. "Getting them here and keeping them in line at the end of a gun is another matter."
"No small feat," Watts agreed.
Caine smiled without humor, reaching for a bottle of ether out of his own travel pouch. He unstopped the cork and doused a rag with the contents.
"Starting with these lads right here," he whispered as the footfalls of approaching marines grew louder.
Moments later, Caine had bested the patrol, reducing them to a breadcrumb trail of crumpled ragdolls to be dragged into the shadows with Anastasia’s help. As quickly as the struggles of his last victim grew faint, Caine released the rag from over the man’s mouth and looked to the next job.
Anastasia pointed at the great cogged doors of the hangar, which opened to the cavernous port of the southern dock below. There, the unwitting aircrew was being shepherded off the Vindicator by Bastian Falk, right on schedule. They only had to clear a path to the dock now.

name: Name
body:
"Caine." A soft man’s voice whispered from the dark.
Caine turned sharply to his name, his nerves at once turned to ice. He knew that voice too well. Indeed, a slender man in grey moved in those shadows, alone yet confident by stride.
"Rebald."
"Are you surprised?" Rebald stepped into the light, a dour expression on his narrow face. "You stole Ace as though it were nothing, true to your word. Of course you were coming here next. It was only a matter of time."
"Yeah, sort of gave my plans up with that whole attempt to do this the honest way." Caine tensed, eyes scanning the room as his hands flitted over his holsters.
"Yes, I’m alone." Rebald saw the hesitancy. "It is to both our advantages…for the moment. However, If I’m not back upstairs shortly, you can expect the full military force of this installation to come down on you in short order."
"I’m listening." Caine took a breath, though his heart was racing. Alongside him, Anastasia was silent, nearly frozen.
"Just so we understand each other: I know about Falk." Rebald eyed the pair of them. "He is being watched. He will not leave this place alive unless I allow it."

name: Name
body:
Caine felt his heart pounding faster by the second; Rebald had him. There could no victory here. Falk was his last gambit to be able to pull this operation off. So why hadn’t Rebald pulled the trigger yet? There could only be one answer.
"What do yeh want?" Caine demanded.
"You know damn well what I want." Rebald paced, his eyes locked to Caine’s. "You took something from me."
"That ship has sailed, I’m afraid." Caine tried not to look at Anastasia.  After all, Rebald didn’t know their arrangement. Could he use that?
"What did you do with it?" Rebald snapped.
"Your little book got me what I needed." Caine shrugged. "Let’s leave it at that."
"I see." Rebald studied his face, sizing him up. "Then we’re going to make a deal for this skyship."
"A deal?" Caine coughed. Rebald may as well have sucker-punched him.
"I’ve come to appreciate your tenacity, Allister." Rebald smiled. "I doubt I could truly keep you from this task you’ve set yourself. Even if the alarm were raised, you would likely shoot your way out. I know how these things tend to go."

name: Name
body: Caine smiled as well despite himself. Perhaps the old spymaster had learned something after all. "But this skyship?" Rebald gestured back the way they had come. "This, I can deny you unless we reach an agreement. You were correct in your assessment to the council. You need it, unequivocally." "All right." Caine sighed. This sounded like the Rebald he knew. "What’s on the table?" "There are loose threads you’ve created putting that book into another’s hands." Rebald grew severe. "We will both want them tied off, believe me." "I’m not doing your dirty work again, Rebald." "I’m giving you a chance." Rebald insisted. "I will stand aside. But when you return—if you return—I will own you for as long as it takes to clean up your mess." "Why not just support this mission then?" Caine shook his head, incredulous. "Give me what I asked for in the first place. All of it." "Oh, I’ll take no blame for any part of this madness." Rebald shook his head. "The risk to this ship, your warjack, and anything and anyone else you have compromised, coerced, or conned your way through is yours and yours alone."

name: Name
body:
Caine pursed his lips. This was ever the dance with this man.
"I meant what I said at the council," The spymaster continued. "I don’t expect Cynthia will survive. Even those with the Gift are more often fuel than anything else to Cryx. If you actually find her alive, you may not bear to see what they have done to her."
Caine bristled. "That’s why I have to go."
"Then be quick about it," Rebald said. "Find what hell has in store for you and wreak your vengeance to whatever effect you see fit. Then report back to me."
"Hell of a bargain, Rebald." Just the same, Caine nodded in defeat.
"I’m glad you see it my way. It seems you have a skyship to steal then." Rebald turned to go. "I’d get to it before that patrol you dispatched is reported missing."
Caine watched Rebald vanish into darkness again.
"What just happened?" Anastasia whispered, still watching the shadows after Rebald.
"Oh, I just made a deal with a devil." Caine swallowed hard, looking ahead to the hangar door. "But it’s not the first time."

name: Name
body:
"Then let us make sure he gets his chance to collect," Anastasia said and turned to go.
***

name: Name
body:
The vaulted chamber was dimly lit with smoldering necrotite glowing within the vents of the machine that covered an entire wall.
"You know what this is, don’t you?" Deneghra led them toward the device.
Before her at last was the malevolent pipe organ that Cynthia had heard so many times, filling her with dread. Cynthia saw now what it truly was. A shivering girl like herself, dressed in rags like her own, had been stuffed into a claustrophobic box like a brass wardrobe at the center of the great collection of steampipes and gears. On either side of the horrible machine, the witches turned cranks that rotated a series of cogs, pumping air into a pair of massive bellows, and the device began to play its music.
Cynthia saw now the true horror of the music’s source. As the bellows filled, incandescent green light bathed the forlorn girl within the box. At once, she vomited, struggling against the chains that bound her limbs. Cynthia tried to look away, but Deneghra gripped her head and turned it to face the prisoner.

name: Name
body:
The girl in the press box was dying, edged closer to death with every gust from the machine’s bellows. A vice from above and below was slowly compressing the space in the box as the organ played, crushing her like an orange in a juice press. She could not scream; her mouth sobbed open unable to take in a breath to exhale. No sound came out. And then, a strand of luminous green slithered painfully from the girl’s chest, coalescing into a small glowing sphere that rose toward the ceiling. Above the pipes, a perforated cylinder waited to draw in the wobbling ball of light.
"It…is her soul…" Cynthia gasped.
"Yes. Can you feel it?" Deneghra reached forward, scooping at the luminescent trail lingering between the rising sphere and the dead girl. It rippled to her touch like water. Cynthia could feel the girl’s life energy leaving her, her raw essence rising up into the funnel of a collection point in the ceiling. In that moment, Cynthia felt the arcane power within her respond,  an invisible tendril reaching out to touch it.

name: Name
body:
"Yes!" At once Deneghra turned, sensing the connection. "That’s it… Do you feel the power it grants? Be saved!"
"I can’t." Cynthia fought back her Gift, pushed it down—or tried to. Determined as she was, in her weakened state, the warmth of the soul felt so inviting. She could even taste it on her tongue, nauseatingly sweet. As she lingered over the connection, she felt impressions of the girl, a communion of sorts. She was a year older, Ordic. Her name was Elise. She was terrified, begging for help…and the taste…so tempting…
"No." Cynthia clenched her teeth again, resisting the impulses of her arcane Gift, pushing it all the way back down, burying it in the depths of her being.
Her anger spurred her on now, gave her the strength to act as she knew she must. Strength enough to open her hand quickly, to slip the key at Deneghra’s belt, as sly as she’d been on her best days in the market. This would be enough. Deneghra did not see her do it, lost as she was in sampling Elise’s essence as it wafted up and away; indeed, her clouded eyes were rolled back into her lifeless head, rapturous.

name: Name
body: No, a stolen key would not be enough to save Elise. Cynthia knew this. Indeed, as the vice of the press box compressed fully at last, the girl who had been Elise was now pulp, oozing through the grates of the hatch. Her spatter struck them both in a warm spray. Cynthia could not help but vomit, her bile splashing at Deneghra’s feet. "You failed." Cynthia coughed, watching as the soul that was Elise vanished at last up into the ceiling pipe, on to its final destination. With a feral growl, she closed off her arcane senses, extinguishing the depraved instincts growing within. "Foolish girl," Deneghra hissed, her elation replaced in an instant with fury. "Make no mistake. If you will not feed, you will be the next one in the box." *** Caine felt seasick, but he knew it was something more. He heaved over the railing of the barge as it plowed through the heavy seas of the Scharde Islands and the slowly thickening haze. He glanced up with no small amount of wonder at the Wind Sabre, tethered to the wide, flat deck of the larger sea vessel. Falk was already aboard the skyship with his press-ganged crew, all of them busily preparing the craft for flight. If he hadn’t fled Sentinel Point aboard the ship, he still wouldn’t believe it could actually fly. A strange sight it was, one ship stacked on top of another.

name: Name
body: To the aft of the barge, another strange sight: Ryan was fraternizing with the ship’s captain, their first recruit for the mission. It seemed there was always some reason for the pair to be in proximity, but then Caine saw his hand on her hips for just a moment, hers briefly on his arm. Caine shook his head; Watts was bloody right about the two of them. Whatever he was saying, he had Ryan’s full attention. "Saying their good-byes, I expect." A dour Watts remarked in passing with a tip of his tricorn before climbing the ladder up to the Sabre. Above them both, the skydrive of the Wind Sabre could be heard as much as felt, its signature hum resonating through the tethers to the deck below Caine’s feet. "How are you feeling, my friend?" Falk leaned over the rail above Caine. "If I’m honest, I think I prefer flying." Caine wiped his mouth. "Never mind me." "I will then." Falk smiled. "She’s all prepped to fly." Caine cracked his neck. "I’ll get the others." He walked over to Ace, who was tied down just behind the skyship to prevent any possibility of being swept overboard. The curved plate armature of his left arm reached out with a fist aimed in Caine’s direction, and he met it halfway. Ace’s mind sensed his own with a cocked head, questioning.

name: Name
body: "Yes, it’s time to board." Caine tried to smile as he unhooked the warjack’s tie-downs. "You ready for this?" Ace shrugged, his piston-driven shoulders heaving comically. "You joker." Caine perked up, patting his warjack by the arm and beckoning toward the Wind Sabre’s gangway. "Up you go then." In short order, Bailoch was roused from his bunk and gathered with the others atop the skyship’s deck. Anastasia was already waiting on the prow of the Sabre, a cool look in her eyes. Above them all, the light of a pale full moon was slowly being choked off by the sooty haze that hung off the coast of Cryx. "Right. Yeh’ve already heard everything there is to say about this mission." Caine paced, unsure of his next words. "We’ve been over it backward and forward, so I’ll not lecture you again. All I can offer now is my thanks, whatever the reason yer here. This place may take us all, and there’s no coin I can offer yeh in that case." A general murmur of sobriety ran through them. "That said," Caine looked forward, "I ain’t never been part of a more fearsome squad than this. Toruk’s scales would be shivering if he knew what was coming."

name: Name
body: Nervous laughs, nods of agreement, and hushed resolve answered him. Caine’s nausea subsided once the Wind Sabre rose off the deck of the barge. The skyship had a manner of its own as it glided through the air, with occasional bumps or sudden altitude corrections, but it was a far smoother ride than being on the water. His stomach relieved, all that remained now was the pall of nagging fear. These stakes were as big as he’d ever played for. It was as simple as that, and he knew it. He watched as the Sabre plowed through the haze, eventually rising over it. The horizon became a cottony blanket before them, riven at turns by the jagged peaks of Cryx. The barge would stay well back of the island’s treacherous waters and its many patrols, ready to recover them once they had Cynthia safely in hand. When Falk at last gave him the signal that they were nearing Skell, Caine noted a particularly foul looking trio of peaks that jutted up through the cloud cover beneath them. He nodded, swallowed, and gathered his team midship by the starboard rail.

name: Name
body: "About the drop," Caine shouted to be heard over the Wind Sabre’s skydrive and high winds alike. "What do you mean drop?" Bailoch eyed Caine suspiciously, working the action of his rifle for a final check. "Ain’t you said we’re coming in for a landing?" "I said, ‘when we make landfall.’ But we can’t risk being spotted by dropping the ship below cloud cover." Caine smiled disarmingly. "I’ve got something else in mind, but I’ll need yeh to stay close to me." "What are ya talking about?" Now even Watts was frowning. "I’m going to bring us down over a series of short jumps. If I get it right, we hit the ground like it’s no more than a ten-foot drop, and they never see us coming beside." "If you get it right? What if you get it wrong?" Ryan demanded. The anxious murmurs exchanged within the group threatened the team’s cohesion. Caine waved them down. "Easy now, I’ve been practicing." It wasn’t a lie, but neither was Caine completely sure. It wouldn’t be the first time he’d pushed his Gift, but certainly, it would be the most people and equipment he’d ever moved: no less than five successive jumps with zero margin for error whatsoever. He did his best to sell his words, yet everyone’s unease remained. "Like I said, stay close."

name: Name
body: Ace immediately stepped next to him, just as they had rehearsed. This prompted the remaining team to pull in as well, even jostling for space. Caine looked at each of them in turn, satisfied by their proximity. "Hell’s coming to Cryx for once." He grinned. "For Cynthia." In a flash of spiraling runes, the deck of the Wind Sabre was empty. END PART 1
